questions.q: Which Gazebo version is paired with ROS 2 Jazzy?
questions.explain: Harmonic is the LTS pair for Jazzy; Classic reached end of support in January 2025.

questions.q: Which sim_vehicle.py arguments are needed for Gazebo?
questions.explain: The frame must contain gazebo-, the model must be JSON.

options: Tells Gazebo where to look for plugins
Sets the path to SDF worlds
Enables lockstep between SITL and the world
questions.explain: Without it Gazebo won't find ArduPilotPlugin — the vehicle gets no physics.
@ is both directions, [ is from Gazebo to ROS, ] is from ROS to Gazebo.

questions.q: Why lockstep between Gazebo and SITL?
options: To speed up camera rendering in the world
Time stays synchronized, even at RTF < 1
questions.explain: The simulation waits for the autopilot — slower, but correct.

questions.q: How do you launch Gazebo for a headless test?
questions.explain: -s is server only, -r starts the simulation right away.

questions.q: How does HITL differ from SITL?
options: In HITL the motors spin on the bench instead of being simulated
A real flight controller, sensors from the simulator
HITL works only in Gazebo Classic
questions.explain: It tests the real hardware: timing, drivers, CPU load.

questions.q: Why can vision from simulation fail in the field?
options: Gazebo can't simulate cameras at all
A perfect image with no noise or blur
Cameras in the field are always worse
questions.explain: You need sensor noise, lighting, blur and testing on real recordings.
